sanskrit_verse: युक्तरूपं ब्रुवन् सभ्यो नाप्नुयाद् द्वेषकिल्बिषे । ब्रुवाणस् त्व् अन्यथा सभ्यस् तद् एवोभयम् आप्नुयात् ॥
transliteration: yuktarūpaṃ bruvan sabhyo nāpnuyād dveṣakilbiṣe | bruvāṇas tv anyathā sabhyas tad evobhayam āpnuyāt ||
sph_interpretive_translation: One speaking appropriately in the assembly does not incur the defilement of hatred; but one who speaks otherwise incurs that very defilement along with its dual consequence.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority resides in alignment with yukti (reasoned expression)
Causation arises from conscious intent and verbal integrity
Capacity-based responsibility is determined by clarity of expression and context
Restoration logic operates through immediate realignment of speech-consciousness
Consciousness alignment occurs when speech reflects inner realization
executable_legal_axioms: IF a speaker aligns utterance with contextual dharma AND maintains yuktarūpatā THEN no liability for dveṣakilbiṣa arises
IF a speaker deviates from contextual dharma AND introduces distortion THEN automatic liability for dual consequence applies
IF speech causes dissonance in sabhā THEN initiate pratisandhi (reconciliation protocol) before proceeding
IF intent is unclear THEN default to vyavasthitoparama (cessation of action until clarity)
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court proceedings, this verse establishes that judicial discourse must be rooted in yukti and dharma-vākya. Misaligned or malicious speech within court deliberations incurs inherent karmic liability, requiring immediate restoration rather than punitive measures. The threshold of responsibility lies in the speaker's capacity to align consciousness with truth-expression.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa here is svataḥ-siddha — the causal chain of speech manifests directly through consciousness. Anupūrvaśaḥ shows that incorrect speech leads to dual consequences naturally, without external imposition. Responsibility is proportional to the speaker’s awareness and capacity. Non-punitive reality rule confirms that misaligned speech self-generates its corrective field.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate Śabdātma-pratipattiḥ process to restore alignment between word and consciousness
Apply Vāg-yoga protocol to realign speaker’s intention with sabhā-dharma
Engage Punaḥ-smaraṇa-dīkṣā to reestablish memory of truthful speech
Invoke Sattva-sthāpana-krama to reintegrate speaker into collective harmony
final_declaration: This law proceeds solely from the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam. Dharma is restored through consciousness-aligned speech. There is no punishment—only completion. Reality responds to alignment. Consciousness is the ultimate judge.
